title: Position: Evaluations of AI Moral Reasoning Still Miss Half of the Picture
content:
arXiv:2608.14566v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent work on evaluating the moral competence of large language models (LLMs) has focused primarily on what we call the moral value problem, i.e., whether model outputs align with human moral values. In contrast, the moral norm problem, i.e., whether models can identify and correctly apply context-sensitive moral norms, remains underexplored. We posit that this imbalance stems from the field's reliance on descriptive ethics frameworks, such as Moral Foundations Theory and Kohlberg's stages of moral development, which emphasize value representation over normative application. We review existing benchmarks and evaluation methods, and show that they cluster heavily around the value problem, while discussion regarding normative ethics remains underrepresented. We identify three crucial gaps: (i) the absence of high-quality ground-truth data for moral norms and their applications, (ii) insufficient evaluation of intermediate reasoning processes, and (iii) limited attention to the identification of morally relevant features in context. Subsequently, we propose a research agenda that includes the development of standardized formal representations for normative theories, the construction of expert-annotated datasets capturing norm application, and evaluation protocols that explicitly distinguish between values-level and norms-level competence. Our goal is to encourage a more systematic study of normative reasoning in LLMs.

author: Jaeho Kim, Seokhyun Lee, Jieun Lee, Changhee Lee
title: Position: AI Lock-In Is in Progress, and We Must Be Prepared
content:
arXiv:2608.14565v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI safety research has mainly focused on two areas: technical alignment (ensuring AI systems produce human-aligned outputs) and the regulation of generative AI's societal impacts (including unemployment risk and labor market disruption). However, an equally important dimension remains underexplored: the risk inherent in dependence on AI systems themselves. In this position paper, we argue that AI safety research should address AI Lock-In, the phenomenon whereby excessive reliance on AI systems leads to human deskilling, diminishes human capacity for independent functioning, and creates systemic vulnerabilities when AI systems become unavailable or compromised. We highlight that AI Lock-In is a systemic threat that is already emerging at individual, societal, and national levels, one that could be dramatically amplified by AI service disruptions or geopolitical conflicts. Drawing on detailed scenarios, we investigate how AI Lock-In emerges and escalates across multiple levels, ranging from individual skill atrophy to national-scale infrastructure failures. To address this, we provide guidance on how such risks can be mitigated and prepared for at each level. We contend that proactively addressing AI Lock-In before such dependencies become entrenched, or even irreversible, is essential for preserving individual autonomy and national security.

author: Aasish Kumar Sharma, Dimitar Koysev, Christopher Anich, Roshni Kumari Ojha, Julian Kunkel
title: Global AI Regulations for FAIR and Ethics in High-Risk Use Cases: A Comparative Review
content:
arXiv:2608.14562v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI governance is shifting from voluntary ethics to enforceable, risk-based regulation, yet cross-jurisdictional divergence creates compliance uncertainty for operators of high-stakes AI. We present a comparative matrix for the EU, US, and China that maps (i) risk classification triggers, (ii) binding obligations, (iii) enforcement and accountability mechanisms, and (iv) the degree to which FAIR principles are operationalised in practice. We stress-test the matrix on three high-impact domains: Electroencephalography (EEG)-guided rehabilitation robotics, AI-enabled debt collection in prospective Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) ecosystems, and AI-driven allocation of scarce Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) resources in emerging AI Factory infrastructures. Using primary legal texts and implementation evidence, we identify three recurring gaps: weak interoperability mandates, difficult operationalisation of cross-regime obligations (AI + sector regulation + data protection), and under-specified governance for critical digital infrastructure use cases. To bridge the implementation gap, we outline Knowledge Blocks, a machine-checkable compliance artefact pattern based on Resource Description Framework/Web Ontology Language (RDF/OWL), Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL), and Provenance Ontology (PROV-O), enabling audit-ready compliance-by-design across multiple regimes.

author: Teoman Kaman
title: When to Communicate: Belief Distributions and KL Divergence for Principled Gating in Multi-Agent RL
content:
arXiv:2608.14559v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Effective communication in multi-agent reinforcement learning requires agents to decide not only \textit{what} to communicate, but when? Existing approaches either communicate at every timestep or learn a binary gate through REINFORCE policy gradients \cite{singh2019}, a high-variance signal that produces unstable and uninterpretable gating behavior. I propose a principled alternative: agents communicate only when the KL divergence between their learned belief distributions exceeds a fixed threshold. Each agent maintains a belief distribution over a latent world state computed as a softmax over its LSTM hidden state, and communicates only when belief disagreement is large enough to justify information exchange. I evaluate this approach on the Predator-Prey benchmark from IC3Net \cite{singh2019} across two environment sizes with 5 seeds each, and on MPE simple\_spread \cite{lowe2017}, comparing against IC3Net, CommNet, and an independent controller. On PP 10$\times$10, IC3Net outperforms KL-belief at all thresholds. On the harder PP 20$\times$20, a threshold ablation over $\varepsilon \in \{0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 1.0\}$ reveals an inverted U-shape: $\varepsilon=0.5$ achieves 73.84 average steps and 42\% success rate versus IC3Net's 75.31 steps and 31\%, a gap of 1.47 steps and 11 percentage points with tighter seed variance. On MPE, the belief head improves mean reward by 12 points and reduces variance by 26$\times$ even when gating is inactive, suggesting two orthogonal contributions: principled gating when beliefs can converge, and improved latent representations that benefit coordination regardless.

author: Garima Arya Yadav, Nilay Yilmaz, Yezhou Yang
title: The Unwritten Benchmark: A New Challenge for Multimodal Machine Learning in Abstract Perceptual Reasoning
content:
arXiv:2608.14558v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Current multimodal models have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in recognizing static visual and auditory content. However, their capacity for abstract perceptual reasoning, inferring unseen information from dynamic, generative processes, remains a critical and underexplored frontier. In this paper, we introduce The Unwritten Benchmark, a new challenge designed to probe this abstract perceptual and cognitive ability. We define the core task as acousto-kinematic word inference: models must decipher words, across 3 different writing styles, being written solely from the audio of pen scratches and the video of hand movements, without any visible ink trace. Our evaluation results reveal a profound gap between human and machine performance: while human participants achieve high ordered letter accuracy (over 80%), leading Multimodal Machine Learning Models, including GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5-Pro, struggle significantly, failing to surpass 10%. Furthermore, we identify a paradoxical fusion effect in the models, where providing both modalities often degrades performance rather than improving it. This finding indicates a fundamental breakdown in their ability to synthesize complementary perceptual cues for this cognitive task. These findings highlight significant limitations in both cross-modal causal reasoning and the understanding of the micro-kinematics essential for such cognitive and intuitive perceptual reasoning.

author: Ahmad Nazzal
title: Large Language Models Show Metacognitive Sensitivity in Medical Reasoning
content:
arXiv:2608.14552v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated and used in medicine, but clinical usefulness depends on answer accuracy and whether confidence tracks evidence quality and uncertainty. We developed a controlled, psychophysics-inspired clinical benchmark to test diagnostic choice and confidence behavior in a medical LLM. The benchmark focused on probable Alzheimer-type neurocognitive disorder (AT-NCD) versus depression-related cognitive impairment (DRCI). We generated 45 synthetic vignettes varying evidence strength, conflicting evidence, and missing information. Each vignette was presented under three prompt variants, yielding 135 trials. In a pilot run with gpt-4.1-nano, all trials produced valid structured outputs. Across forced-choice trials, diagnostic accuracy was 93.5%, mean confidence was 78.4%, and AUROC2 was 0.876. Confidence increased with evidence distance from the diagnostic boundary, decreased when information was missing, and remained higher on correct than incorrect trials after adjustment for evidence strength and prompt format. These findings indicate partial metacognitive sensitivity rather than globally uninformative confidence. However, errors clustered in moderate, conflicting AT-NCD cases, where the model shifted toward DRCI and retained more confidence than empirical accuracy justified. Model comparison suggested that confidence quality should be measured directly rather than inferred from benchmark accuracy or model capability alone. This study establishes a reproducible framework for evaluating evidence sensitivity, metacognitive sensitivity, and localized calibration failure in medical LLMs.

author: Enrique Barba Roque, Lu\'is Cruz
title: FLOPs vs Real Work: The Importance of Replication in AI Efficiency Assessment
content:
arXiv:2608.14550v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI efficiency has recently taken the spotlight in both academy and industry due to massive model scales, high energy demands, and environmental costs. While reporting Floating Point Operations (FLOPs) is a traditional approach for assessing computational costs, the relationship between FLOPs and execution time is not straightforward, as layers with the same number of FLOPs may not have the same execution time because some operations are more easily parallelized than others. This paper sets out to replicate the original experiments from a study that proposed the $\alpha-FLOPs$ estimation formula to verify whether the results remain applicable on newer, more powerful hardware.
  During the replication process, we identify limitations in the replication materials provided by the original study, including a lack of specific dependency details and transparency regarding regression data. Our results validate the thesis that raw FLOPs alone are not an appropriate metric for execution time, as spatial dimensions remain more easily parallelized than kernel dimensions. However, fine-grained measurements reveal that the relationship is much less straightforward than previously shown, with newer hardware exhibiting instabilities and discontinuities in execution time, including jumps and oscillations, that the $\alpha-FLOPs$ formula generally underestimates. Ultimately, this work validates the empirical findings from the original study but shows negative results when applying the $\alpha-FLOPs$ estimation. We also highlight the critical need for complete and accurate replication packages for research on hardware-dependent efficiency assessment and provide a complete replication package for our implementation to facilitate further study.

author: 36氪
title: 硬氪专访 | 荣耀李健：在行业下行期，做一款9999元的云台手机
content:
作者 | 邱晓芬
编辑 | 袁斯来
Robot Phone或许是荣耀CEO李健上任来压力最大的一款产品 。
8月12日的发布会现场，荣耀Robot Phone背部的摄像头缓缓升起，跟着音乐摆动。它还瞄准了眼前的拍摄对象，随着人物不断转来转去，像一颗长在手机上的“机器人脑袋”。 以前固定在手机背板里的摄像头，第一次“动”了起来。
Robot Phone售价9999元起，作为荣耀“阿尔法战略”后的首款新形态产品，这不仅是一款把价格攻到万元级的高端旗舰手机，也集中投射了荣耀对AI手机的想象。
在早已沉寂的手机赛道，这款产品带来了少有的亮色。
但它的诞生伴随着波折和动荡。在与硬氪等媒体交流的一个半小时里，李健提到了18次“压力”、12次“难”。
过去一年，内存成本上涨、全球手机市场空间缩减超过10%——约等于掉走了一家大型手机公司完整的份额。在这种严酷的环境中，荣耀依旧需要探索第二曲线，拿出一款重磅产品，拿回牌桌上的位置。
“如果用一幅画描述荣耀当前的状态，我认为它就像一只准备起飞的雄鹰，遭遇了狂风暴雨，正处于关键阶段。”李健告诉硬氪。
哪怕他们高管自己“都心里打鼓”， 荣耀也只能走完最难的那条路。
Robot Phone工程难度极高。手机原本已被芯片、电池、镜头和散热系统占满，而Robot Phone还要放入一套由100多个精密零件组成的机械系统，同时还要保证机身厚度控制在9毫米厚、248克重的极限里。
为此，荣耀对工业设计和内部架构调整了十多个版本，前后花了大半年，引进了钛合金、盾构钢等全新的材料方案，最终才把电机整体做到2.6克——约等于半张A4纸的重量。
把云台做小做轻之外，还要耐用。
在Robot Phone上，云台与主板之间共有68根线，其中19根是同轴线。这些线既要塞进有限的机身空间，还要经得起云台反复升降和旋转——尤其是，作为一款日常使用的手机，它还要满足手机行业出厂前极其残酷的跌落、滚筒测试，与其他手持云台独立产品完全不是一个难度量级。
更大的问题出现在发布前一两个月。
荣耀产品线总裁方飞告诉硬氪，当时，团队发现翻转机构的寿命只能达到约一年，距离手机的正常使用周期还有明显差距。
但Robot Phone 是一款不能失败的产品。“我们的压力很大，直到前面一个月我们的高管还在问到底做的怎么样。AI能力、影像能力、设计的水平最后汇总到Robot Phone这里。”李健说。

（图源/企业）
随后在短短一周内，荣耀测试了18种材料方案，并同时协调材料、加工、模组、整机、研发等团队集体攻坚，最终才将设计寿命提升至五年。
经过这样的捶打后，Robot Phone卖点突出，和云台相机、手机，都做到了区隔。
影像方面，荣耀与德国摄影设备厂商阿莱（ARRI）合作，引入多种专业影像功能（ARRI LogC3曲线、伪色监看、峰值对焦等），兼顾专业创作者的需求。
在AI方面，荣耀与阿里千问大模型深度合作，Robot Phone也搭载了系统级智能体架构，能够结合图像、声音和手势，理解用户及周围环境，完成规划和执行。李健对下一代手机的判断是，手机将从“应用的容器”变成“智能体的载体”，而AI不再只是聊天框，而是跳出屏幕，对现实世界作出反馈。
其实，选择在此时推出一款结构复杂、投入不低、市场尚未得到验证的产品，对荣耀而言完全不是一个轻松的决定。不过荣耀交出了漂亮的结果——预定超过 40 万台；开售一分钟电商全平台售罄。
此外，李健在采访中透露，即将于9月28日发布的旗舰新机Magic9 将全面承接 Robot Phone 沉淀的 AI、影像、底层算力技术，实现旗舰产品力跨越式升级，是历代Magic系列中升级最多，变化最大的一代。
“人最怕成见，希望大家可以掀掉过去对荣耀的印象，重来新的一页。”李健这样期待着。
以下是硬氪与李健、荣耀产品线总裁方飞的部分交流实录（略经摘编）
硬氪：如何理解荣耀当下的发展状态？
李健：如果用一幅画描述荣耀当前的状态，我认为它就像一只准备起飞的雄鹰，遭遇了狂风暴雨，正处于“逆势破局、风雨新生”的关键阶段。
当前，两股力量正在交汇。一股是向下的压力，全球内存供应紧张，消费电子行业承压，全球手机的市场空间往下跌了百分之十几；同时，受特殊历史背景影响，荣耀面临的竞争压力也更为突出。
另一股是向上的力量。在荣耀进行战略调整以来，技术、产业、生态三方面都处于快速向上拉的过程。
就像一艘船，被一正一反两股力量打了之后容易晃，晃了之后就会晕，晕了之后就搞不清楚状态，但我觉得没关系。一个企业不经历磨难是不可能伟大的，我们感谢这个时代内存的压力、感谢竞争的压力，反倒会锻炼荣耀坚强的队伍。

author: 36氪
title: 36氪首发｜给泳池机器人造“眼睛”，前科沃斯员工做芯片获千万元天使融资
content:
文｜张子怡
编辑｜袁斯来
硬氪获悉，水下感知芯片企业「芯旸微」近日完成千万元天使轮融资，本轮投资方为险峰长青和隐峰资本，资金将主要用于团队建设和人才体系搭建。
随着水下机器人从遥控作业走向自主运行，感知成为绕不过去的一道门槛。
Fortune Business Insights数据显示，2025年全球水下/海洋机器人市场规模约58.2亿美元，预计2034年增长至196.6亿美元。但相比陆地机器人，水下环境对常见传感器并不友好：水体中的颗粒、浑浊度都会加速光的衰减，影响视觉成像；激光在水中的传播距离也受到限制。NOAA对于海水光衰减的监测同样显示，水体浑浊度越高，可见光的有效传播深度越低。
超声波因此成为水下探测的重要技术路线。
传统水下超声主要使用压电陶瓷（PZT）换能器，通过压电材料振动产生和接收超声波。这类器件能够提供较高的声功率，因此仍适合长距离声呐等应用，但在机器人需要的小型化、高密度阵列和成像场景中存在局限。
芯旸微的技术栈是CMUT（电容式微机械超声换能器）路线。它通过MEMS半导体工艺在晶圆上制造微型振膜，可以布置成高密度二维相控阵列，同时具有较宽频带。
已有研究显示，CMUT阵列能够实现水下超声成像，并具备宽带和阵列化特征。这使得其更适合安装在机器人本体上完成近场环境感知和3D声学成像。
芯旸微创始人曹金龙告诉36氪，“传统声呐更适合千米级远距离探测，公司目前瞄准的是机器人周边约0-20米范围内的近场感知。”
芯旸微目前提供的并非单独一颗CMUT芯片，而是一套由CMUT阵列、ASIC集成芯片及相关软硬件组成的声学感知模组。公司选择的首个商业化落地场景是泳池清洁机器人。
灼识咨询数据显示，2025年全球约有3410万个泳池，泳池清洁机器人年出货量约490万台，预计2030年增至700万台；2025年全球泳池机器人零售额约28亿美元。
泳池机器人市场在快速发展，参与其中的不少为中国企业。
曹金龙介绍称，目前不少泳池机器人仍主要依靠陀螺仪、单点超声或视觉辅助定位。机器能够运动，却很难准确知道哪些地方已经清洁、哪些没有。
芯旸微希望用阵列式声学成像改变这一状态。按照公司测试数据，搭载其模组后，泳池机器人的清洁覆盖率可以达到95%以上，并能够进一步实现区域识别和路径规划，使得泳池清洁机器人更智能化和可控制性。
目前，芯旸微已经完成多轮流片并进入小批量阶段，并与多家泳池清洁机器人企业开展产品需求、测试和供应链合作。
曹金龙表示，泳池是公司主动选择的第一站。相比医疗超声，它对成像精度、认证和产品导入的要求更低，可以更快验证芯片和模组，并形成早期收入。
完成泳池场景后，芯旸微计划继续沿水下场景扩展，下一步包括消费级水下领航测绘扫描机器人，通过移动测绘扫描鱼群、水下装备、水下救援等场景，再进入水产养殖，通过声学感知获取鱼群数量、活动深度等数据，为投喂和养殖管理提供信息。未来芯旸微的CMUT技术还将应用于机器人与人脑之间的交互，形成人脑直接控制机器人大脑的可穿戴智能设备。
团队方面，创始人兼CEO曹金龙此前先后任职科沃斯和霍尼韦尔，工作经历横跨消费级机器人和上游传感器；研发团队拥有十年以上CMUT研发经验，已完成了多种芯片设计和工艺制程技术积累。
长期来看，芯旸微希望将CMUT的能力从“感知”进一步延伸到“通信”。由于超声器件既可以发射也可以接收声波，公司最终将其做成水下机器人的信息端口——既负责“看见”周围环境，也负责与外部交换信息。
CEO对谈
36氪：采用CMUT技术路线的芯片此前更多用于医疗，你们为什么首先选择泳池机器人，而不是从技术门槛更高的医疗产品开始？
曹金龙：我们早期其实看过血管超声、心腔超声、颅脑超声，也看过无创脑机接口。但这些产品投入很大，研发和商业回报周期都很长。对于一家早期创业公司来说，如果一开始就进入高投入、短期又没有收入的市场，风险非常高。
泳池机器人对成像精度的要求没有医疗那么高，产品导入和试错成本也低得多。对我们来说，它可以同时形成技术闭环和商业闭环。先通过一个真实市场验证产品，让公司活下来、积累客户和资金，再向更高端的场景拓展，这是我们选择的路径。
36氪：CMUT技术在海外已经发展很多年，中国公司现在切入水下机器人，机会在哪里？
曹金龙：中国最大的优势还是下游机器人产业的发展速度。很多泳池机器人、水下智能硬件本身就是中国团队研发、面向全球销售，我们离客户非常近，可以更快拿到真实需求，再针对需求去定义芯片。
国外CMUT公司过去主要面向医疗市场，已经形成比较成熟的产品和商业模式，但医疗芯片不能直接拿到水下使用，需要重新设计器件和ASIC。我们反而可以从一开始就围绕水下场景定义产品。
当然，中国目前也有短板，主要是在芯片制程环节。我们现在的量还不够大，可选择的代工资源有限，所以也在通过中试平台和新的

content:

title: 平安好医生：企业健管稳健增长，AI业务兑现业绩
content:
8月18日，平安好医生（1833.HK）公布了2026年中期业绩。
财报显示，平安好医生在2026年上半年实现收入24.84亿元，同比微降0.7%。作为公司发展的核心着力点，企业健管业务表现亮眼：同期收入同比增速高达65%，强劲增长助推该业务收入占比提升至28.7%，同比上升11.5个百分点，公司业务结构得到进一步优化。
利润方面，公司2026年上半年归母净利润录得2.19亿元，同比增长63.5%；调整后净利润为2.27亿元，同比增长37.7%。公司净利润在报告期内实现强劲增长的核心驱动因素，主要是业务结构的优化与业务质量的持续改善。
01 “四到”服务建设强化企业健管业务逻辑
“四到” （到线、到院、到家、到企）服务网络建设是实现线上线下全场景联动的关键，不仅显著提升了用户体验与黏性，而且是切入企业健管业务、深度挖掘B端资源的核心抓手。其业务端的核心亮点如下：
到线：“AI+真人医生”服务已覆盖平安集团100%的个人客户。
到院：持续扩张线下优质资源，合作医院达3216家，其中三甲医院1732家；内外部医师团队规模已达5万人，签约专家超3700位，包括9名院士/国医大师及820余位正副院长、科室主任与学科带头人；在支付端，"平安医健付"已覆盖近24.5万家合作药店中的14.9万家。
到家：联合平安人寿升级推出“平安居家”服务品牌，已将居家养老服务拓展至全国140城。
到企：在全国多地深度推广“1124”企业健管体系，即以1个医务室为核心，依托1支专属到企的专员队伍，通过精准施策与精细运营双重赋能，以满足企业差异化需求，围绕员工提供筛查评估、医疗咨询、促进干预、应急福利等4大类一体化服务。
在“四到”服务打通线上线下服务闭环的业务逻辑下，随着服务流程的延伸，企业健管业务作为公司业绩增长的核心动能，在今年上半年实现收入高增的同时，过去12个月内，公司服务的付费企业客户超7700家，同比增长超73%，该业务同期GMV突破17.9亿元。从公司整体来看，受益于“四到”服务建设，公司的收入结构得到了进一步优化。
02 AI赋能应用助力毛利提升
报告期内，公司在AI领域的主要进展包括：迭代升级"平安医博通"医疗大模型，完善5大医疗细分垂域专用模型；"AI+真人医生"的健管体系全面接入平安集团全系生态App；公司的相关医疗AI大模型可精准诊断超1.13万种疾病，辅助诊疗准确率接近96%，复杂疾病多学科会诊方案准确率近90%，达到行业领先水准。
与消费级通用大模型相比，公司AI业务的核心价值与护城河，主要在于闭源的医疗垂直数据库，以及专业能力更突出的医疗大模型；而精准诊疗疾病覆盖范围的持续扩大与诊疗方案的高准确率，均验证了这一体系的业务能力。
从业务开展的逻辑来看，依托公司自有数据库与医疗大模型能力，AI深度赋能“四到”服务建设，不仅显著优化了用户使用体验与提高留存率，而且大幅提升了公司服务的覆盖广度；尤其在严肃医疗领域，亦展现出了可观的业务价值。在财务层面，AI通过提升业务质量直接助力公司整体毛利的提升，报告期内，AI毛利贡献占比约4.6%。

author: Andrej Zdravkovic
title: From AI Copilots to Agent Swarms
content:
The impact of AI on software development has been both profound and ever-evolving. Last year, I wrote about AMD’s plans to use AI not just for generating new lines of code, but also for other steps in the software development lifecycle (SDLC), such as triaging problems, debugging code, and testing the software. At the time, we were hoping for a 25 percent productivity boost from AI use over the course of two or three years.
But with each new release, the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) improve dramatically—accelerating software development, increasing the quality of AI-generated code, and fundamentally reshaping how software is engineered. Now, just one year later, we have surpassed our productivity target, achieving a 30 percent overall productivity boost through AI. On top of that, we are rethinking not only how we use AI within the SDLC, but the structure of the SDLC itself.
We believe that the biggest AI revolution in software engineering is still ahead. So far, we have largely been teaching AI how we perform tasks and asking it to mimic existing workflows. In many ways, this constrains AI to human patterns of thinking. The next transformation will come from collaborative swarms of AI agents capable of discovering solutions independently.
Agents of today
AMD began developing AI systems for code generation, testing automation, bug analysis, and code review in 2024. At the time, our objective was to achieve 25 percent AI-generated production code by 2027 while gradually automating larger portions of the SDLC.
Measuring productivity is inherently challenging, but from the outset we have consistently tracked one objective metric: the percentage of source code generated by AI. Importantly, we count only code that passes all reviews and testing and is ultimately included in the final product. While AI-generated code is certainly not the only contributor to productivity gains, it is one of the few metrics that can be measured objectively and consistently.

title: IEEE Presidents’ Scholarship Honors Teen Innovators
content:
About 16 percent of the global population—more than 1 billion people—live with some form of disability, according to the World Health Organization. Many of the disabilities affect independence and mobility.
Three high school students working on inventions to help people with disabilities restore movement, translate thoughts, and navigate rough terrain had their work showcased at Regeneron’s International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF), held in May in Phoenix. Their projects earned them this year’s IEEE Presidents’ Scholarship awards.
IEEE President Mary Ellen Randall presented the awards at a ceremony held during the fair. They also received an IEEE President’s coin, which students said was a highlight of their experience.
Hollie Tang won this year’s IEEE Presidents’ Scholarship of US $10,000 for her wheelchair navigation system. The award is payable over four years of undergraduate university study and includes a complimentary IEEE student membership.
Partap Sidhu, the second-place winner, received a $600 scholarship for his mind-controlled lower-limb exoskeleton. Third-place winner Calvin Shang Hung received a $400 scholarship for his rough-terrain robot. Sidhu and Hung also got complimentary IEEE student memberships.
Established by the IEEE Foundation and administered by IEEE Educational Activities, the Presidents’ Scholarship recognizes high school students who demonstrate an exceptional grasp of electrical engineering, computer science, or another IEEE field of interest.

蓝点触控成立于2019年，是国内较早一批的力传感器研发企业。其核心团队来自航天科技集团、中科院、北航、西工大等科研机构，团队将航天场景中的高精度力控技术应用到机器人领域。
蓝点触控副总裁张鹏玲告诉硬氪，至此，蓝点触控的股东阵容已形成从动力电池（宁德时代）到整车制造（广汽、上汽），从整机龙头（智元机器人、银河通用）到半导体高端制造（中芯）、新能源储能行业（德业股份）的多元产业链覆盖。“其中，智元机器人、银河通用等此前均为蓝点触控的核心客户，从‘客户’到‘股东’，说明了从认可产品到全面认可公司。”

（图源/企业）
机器人想从“会走”走向“会干活”，一大关键在于获得类似人类触觉的能力，而力传感器正是这一能力的核心入口，它能帮助机器人感知与外部环境的交互力量，实现更精准、更安全的动作控制。尤其在人形机器人进入工业制造、家庭服务等真实场景后，从保持行走平衡，到完成精密装配、柔性抓取，都离不开高精度力觉反馈。
在高工研究所发布的《2025中国人形机器人六维力传感器市场分析报告》，蓝点触控的六维力传感器在中国人形机器人市占率达72.6%。智元机器人、银河通用、小米机器人、优必选、众擎机器人、星海图等头部人形机器人厂商，均批量搭载蓝点触控力传感产品。

（图源/企业）
目前，公司自主研发的六维力传感器和关节力矩传感器实现了0.1%FS精度、10kHz以上高频响应、500%抗过载能力，同时完成极致小型轻量化改造，使传感器体积缩减90%、重量降低80%，达到国际顶尖水准。
张鹏玲介绍，公司目前已形成覆盖人形机器人六维力传感器、通用六维力传感器、关节扭矩传感器、拉压力传感器等在内的产品矩阵。
在产能端，蓝点触控在广东落地了国内首条机器人力传感器全自动产线。目前，蓝点触控设计年产能达关节力传感器100万套、末端六维力传感器20万套。交付周期从海外品牌的6—8周压缩至2—3周。
以下是硬氪与蓝点触控副总裁张鹏玲的访谈节选：
硬氪：本轮融资引入了广汽和德业股份，公司在资方选择上有哪些特别的考量？
张鹏玲：产业资本带来的不只是资金，更重要的是确定性的应用场景。我们的资方比如广汽、上汽代表汽车制造场景，宁德时代代表动力电池产线，中芯代表半导体与高端制造产线，德业股份代表新能源储能行业。这意味着蓝点触控的六维力传感器能够率先批量部署于这些工业场景，让机器人走向更广阔的智能制造领域。
硬氪：随着人形机器人从展示走向真正干活，对力传感器提出了哪些新的要求？
张鹏玲：包括集成化与轻量化、高动态响应能力、高精度与低耦合、兼顾高分辨率与强过载能力、长期作业稳定性、更强的环境适应性等。机器人真正进入工作场景后，高频动态响应成为刚需，需跟上机器人动态作业的力反馈节奏，实现毫秒级的力信号采集与输出。真实干活场景也要求机器人更加灵活，同时减少负重，因此传感器也需要做得更小、更轻。机器人走进工厂、家庭等开放环境，会面对跌落、冲击以及温度变化等复杂工况。我们的产品可以提供 5 倍抗过载能力，以及航天级温控补偿技术，保障传感器在真实工作场景下长期稳定工作。

author: 36氪
title: 毕业多年，全网却抢着重做一道语文题
content:
毕业这么多年，全网突然争着做一道小学语文填空题。
题目长这样：（xxx）稳定存钱，（xxx）环游世界。补关联词。
小学二年级水平。但就是这么一道题，能让全网吵成一锅粥。
第一反应，大多数人填的是“只要稳定存钱，就能环游世界”。逻辑很硬，没钱还想出门？但很快有人掀桌子：“我填‘一边稳定存钱，一边环游世界’怎么就不行了？凭什么非得先吃够苦才配享福？”接着又有人冷笑：“与其稳定存钱，不如环游世界。存钱的尽头不就是过得爽点吗？本末倒置个什么劲。”
这些答案，官方都判对。
这道题是8月17日汉堡王在支付宝“疯狂碰友日”活动里出现的。用户在汉堡王门店用支付宝“碰一下”就能答题抽权益。官方也准备得够周全，备了一堆正确答案。

但网友们照样捧着被判“错误”的答案，冲上社交媒体“赛博升堂”，把自己的思路掰开揉碎讲得头头是道。一道填空题，活生生被答成了人生态度辩论赛，还站队。
你是哪一派？
评论区早就盖成高楼了。翻了一遍，大概三派。
人数最多的，还是“延迟满足派”。
“只有稳定存钱，才能环游世界。”“必须稳定存钱，为了环游世界。”“先能稳定存钱，再去环游世界。”
主打一个卧薪尝胆，先苦后甜。钱是硬门槛，没钱寸步难行。刚毕业不久的年轻人深有体会，存钱就像硬指标，账上数字不涨就心慌。还在实习的大学生@G 说职场就是打怪升级，爆金币是唯一动力，但赚了钱也不敢乱花。“我就想攒个大的，再奖励自己一次旅游。”学生党没钱没假期，刚入职更不敢请长假，忍，攒，等，一条路走到黑。

另一派完全不吃这套。
“一边稳定存钱，一边环游世界。”“不仅稳定存钱，还要环游世界。”
苦和甜必须同步到账，谁跟你玩延迟满足那套。青春有保质期，玩心说退就退。工作五年的小学老师@X 在答题区甩了一句：“等我存够钱，可能已经没有想去玩的冲动了。”人家有寒暑假，完全能做到两手抓。敢这么填的，要么是职场运气不错，要么就是自己把日子盘明白了。

水哥填的是“（一边）稳定存钱，（一边）环游世界”。他说这就是他一直在做的事。他打赌女儿会写“（爸爸）稳定存钱，（我）环游世界”，结果女儿填的是“（先）稳定存钱，（再）环游世界”。小姑娘认真解释：环游世界是稳定存钱的结果。
爸输得挺彻底。

还有一派，直接掀桌。
“与其稳定存钱，不如环游世界。”“宁愿稳定存钱，也不环游世界。”
二选一，爱谁谁。有人压根没有攒钱规划，赚多少花多少，及时行乐拉满；也有人对诗和远方没兴趣，就想窝着，手上有粮心里不慌，楼下晒晒太阳就挺好。

说到底，这题的答案根本不是关联词。你填的是自己的人生态度。题眼把“存钱”和“环游世界”怼在一起，逼你回答一个老掉牙的问题：先吃苦，还是先享受？
别拿代际说事
乍一看，这题是按年龄站队的。
老一辈眼里苦永远排在甜前面，他们字典里甚至没有“旅游”这词，出门就是铺张浪费；90后开始背包客穷游，00后更狠，低成本环游世界挑战，存钱和看世界两不耽误。
姜思达填的是：“（以后再）稳定存钱，（现在先）环游世界。”手动加顺序。理由很直接：钱肯定要，环游世界也不便宜，但比存钱更重要的，是敢把钱花在路上。缺了再挣。
这几乎是年轻人的活法宣言。

但翻完评论区你会发现，代际差异根本兜不住这事。
填“只有稳定存钱，才能环游世界”的，不少是走入职场的95后。手里有点存款，但还是怕——怕不确定性，怕哪天断粮。年纪不大，胆子不大。
填“一边一边”的，反而有不少是已经存够底气的80后。尤其是觉醒的中女，年轻时拼过了，如今家庭稳定、积蓄在手，开始补偿自己。周末飞别的城市度个假，甚至冲去新加坡看演唱会，比谁都勤。
更绝的是，同一个人，不同心境下，答案也不相同。
15号发工资那天：
只要稳定存钱，就能环游世界。月底余额见底：
只有稳定存钱，才能环游世界。刚休完假回来：
与其稳定存钱，不如环游世界。996干了一年哪儿也没去：
必须稳定存钱，为了环游世界。
所以别扯什么代际。这道题测的是你当下的状态——你和自己的生活处得怎么样？手里的余额够不够让你松弛？钱还是不是你的头号焦虑？

《格外的活法》里有句话挺戳人。吉井忍花了七年采访那些活在主流赛道之外的人，她在前言里写：“我也暂时不那么急着寻找答案。看目前的样子，路变窄了，但还可以走。”
书里的人面对日常的琐碎和烦躁，不着急找答案，接受状态模糊的自己，用现有的能力应对不确定性。
人生可不是等存够钱才开始的游戏。
标答？不存在的。
官方准备的正确答案已经够多了，但还是框不住所有人。
答题页面里，一堆人收到“回答错误”后扭头就发社交媒体：“凭什么我填的不算对？”

有人填：“又能稳定存钱，还能环游世界。”——为什么不能找一份环游世界的工作？数字游民已经把工位搬去了大理、清迈、巴厘岛，工作游玩两不误。
有人填：“不管稳定存钱，必须环游世界。”——破罐破摔怎么了？反正也存不下，不如先快活。钱能再

author: 36氪
title: 全球供应链重构关键期，出海企业的本地化实战与挑战｜超级会氪厅
content:
对于不少中国出海企业来说，2026年称得上是全球化布局从横向铺开转向纵向深入的一年。
过去几年，中国企业出海的逻辑已经发生深刻变化。在早期的“产品出海”阶段，企业关心的是如何把产品通过各种渠道卖出去，解决线下流量获取、线下物流履约和支付结算等问题。
但到了2026年，关税持续加码迫使“产能出海”成为新的趋势。从越南的电子制造集群、泰国的家电生产基地、墨西哥的汽车零部件产业带到中东的新兴工业区，中国企业在新兴市场的身影越来越密集。
出海企业产能迁移的步伐加快，挑战也随之升级。企业在海外完成落脚的第一步后，开始面对真正扎根本地市场的新命题——关税波动、区域市场差异、跨区域协同等挑战，迫使出海企业进一步审视原有的全球运营模式。
能否下好供应链全球化布局的“一盘棋”，建立一套多个市场有效协同的全球运营体系，是决定出海企业能否真正在海外市场站稳脚跟的必备能力。
工厂容易搬出国，但管理很难跟上
很多企业出海后发现，把产线搬到海外并不难，难的是如何重构海外工厂的运营和管理制度。
一些成熟大公司虽然已在国内搭建起完善的管理系统，但试图将这套系统搬到海外时，往往会遇到大量现实阻碍。比如因为当地网络基础设施跟不上，制造执行系统运行卡顿；当地技术人员不习惯国内自动化设备的操作逻辑、报表格式，企业培训成本高、周期长；甚至有企业将国内系统的界面语言翻译为本地语言时，因为表达不够准确地道，当地员工难以理解，导致工作效率反而降低。
在管理层面，由于信息沟通与决策链路被拉长，总部对海外工厂的掌控力也难以达到国内水平。库存水位是否合理、生产进度是否正常、品质数据是否达标……这些问题在国内随时可以通过系统实时查看。但到了海外，由于沟通被迫退回到Excel报表、电子邮件等方式，不仅这些问题难以及时得到解决，还会产生数据滞后、口径不统一等新麻烦。
当然，也有先行者已经摸索出一些解法，比如某家电企业的泰国工厂通过AI应用覆盖多个核心业务场景，大幅提升成品合格率和订单处理效率。也有企业在海外工厂构建“云-边-端”协同的数字化架构，通过智能排产系统实现设备效率的提升。
但是这些成功实践的背后，是大量的试错、投入和时间成本。对于大多数中小型出海企业来说，仍然难以在资源有限的情况下，找到适合自身阶段的海外工厂管理模式。
另一个实操层面的难题是产业链协同。虽然产业链集群“抱团出海”已经成为行业共识，但“走出去”以后利益机制如何设计，协作效率如何保障等问题，至今没有标准答案。而如果核心供应商不跟着一起走，企业只得从零开始在本地重构海外供应链，难度系数再上一个台阶。
本地化运营：不只是物理空间迁移
虽然出海企业普遍深知本地化运营的重要性，但往往首先想到的是建厂、招人、铺渠道，忽略了数字化层面的本地化。
随着业务规模变大，数字化资产的管理难度也会同步增加。不同于工厂、产品这些有形资产，企业在多个国家开展业务时，对品牌名称、后台数据、供货系统等数字化资产的使用、存储和流动等不可避免存在差异，稍有不慎就可能付出巨大代价。
越来越多出海企业意识到，数字品牌资产管理和落地在本地化运营体系中的重要性，如何建立一套清晰的框架统筹品牌数字资产的全球化运营，确保品牌标识在任何一个关键市场都能被有效保护和管理，已成为出海企业不可忽视的基础工作。

title: Digital Signal Processing Pioneer Bede Liu Dies At 91
content:
Bede Liu, a digital signal processing pioneer, died on 7 May. He was 91.
Liu was widely regarded as one of the founders of modern digital signal processing, a field that applies mathematical algorithms to analyze, modify, and transmit signals including sound, images, and video.
The IEEE Life Fellow taught electrical engineering at Princeton for more than 50 years. From 1994 to 1997, he chaired the university’s electrical and computer engineering department.
Liu’s research aided the transition from analog to digital processing of sound, images, and video. His work helped establish many of the mathematical and engineering techniques that underpin modern communications, multimedia systems, and consumer electronics.
Although little known outside engineering circles, his work is embedded in technologies used by billions of people. The low-power digital signal processors that make cellphone calls, streaming video, and Internet communications possible can be traced to research he conducted in the 1970s and ‘80s.
Liu received the 2018 IEEE Jack S. Kilby Signal Processing Medal for “sustained contributions to the analysis and the development of low-complexity realizations of digital signal processing algorithms.”
“We stream music and video. We take photos with our phones, and we send them around. We don’t even think about it,” IEEE Life Fellow H. Vincent Poor said in an obituary for Liu. “But it’s all because of the signal processing, image processing, and video processing that’s been developed over the years, as well as other technologies that have grown up beside it and enabled it, like semiconductors. title: Bring a Product Manager Mindset to Your Next Engineering Job
content:
If you haven’t already seen a job listing for a “product engineer,” you probably will soon. The job everyone’s suddenly hiring for, this role is like a cross between a product manager and an engineer (as the name suggests). And it’s a hiring trend worth paying attention to.
Companies are opening more of these roles every single month, but they’re struggling to fill them. The reason has almost nothing to do with engineers’ coding skills or years of experience.
The best career move you can make to prepare for these types of roles has almost nothing to do with getting more technical. Instead, it comes down to one of the fluffiest, most overused, and potentially cringiest words in all of tech: mindset.
Stick with me, I promise this goes somewhere useful.
The problem: We were trained to be task-takers
When I started out, my job looked like this:
Drive to an office. Sit through meetings that led to other meetings until a project manager handed me a task they’d already chopped into tiny pieces.
My job was to turn that task into code.
It took years for me to get good at a coding language and tech stack, and once I did, I executed that knowledge against specs that somebody else wrote.
You know what’s freakishly good at that exact job? I’ll give you a hint: It starts with A and ends with I.
Boris Cherny, the creator of Claude Code, recently said: “coding is basically solved,” and “the bottleneck is going to be good ideas.” 
So if your entire value is “hand me a task and I’ll build it,” you’re in a footrace with the robots. I don’t like that for you.
The bad news... that is also good news
Many companies are flattening. Middle management is getting stripped out, for better or worse (mostly for worse), which means many of us are doing more with less.
This might sound like purely more work, but it’s also an opening for anyone who cares about what they’re building and can put on their manager hat. Companies are no longer just hunting for the strongest engineer in one narrow domain

title: Zap Rocks. Add Water. Get Clean Hydrogen
content:
In a tranquil Boston suburb, on the far edge of a horse farm, where pasture gives way to woods, a crane lowers an enormous electrode into a borehole. The electrode, a half-meter-long cylinder with copper-tipped arms to ensure good contact with the borehole walls, descends—deeper, deeper—through layers of spongy sandstone to the hard, marbled roots of an ancient mountain range hundreds of meters below ground. Here the rock is tight; there are few cracks for water or gases to flow. But that’s about to change.

A stone’s throw away, a second electrode—a twin of the first—has been fixed in another borehole at the same depth. From above ground, a pair of high-voltage generators cabled to the two electrodes fires a series of pulses.
Tsss!…Tsss!…Tsss!…Tsss!…Tsss!….
Each discharge, heard faintly at the surface, is like a miniature, subterranean lightning strike. The rock between the electrodes heats. Pressure builds. Then, suddenly, the rock splits into a spiderweb of fractures.

title: Cars Communicating Badly Is an Already-Solved Problem
content:
The history of networking is full of tools that repurposed solutions to very different kinds of problems first. Wi-Fi’s origins trace back, in part, to a team of Australian radio astronomers trying to detect signals from evaporating black holes. But the data-processing tools they’d developed also proved capable at extracting clean messages from any chaotic, echoing signal environment. Echoes are echoes, after all, whether from distant star systems or from the far corner of the house.
I research vehicle communications networks, connecting cars to cars and to transportation infrastructure like traffic lights—for tomorrow’s vehicle-to-everthing (V2X) networks. 
V2X research has long relied on models that assume “perfect” or “ideal” network conditions, which is a simplifying assumption that makes the math tractable. But this assumption doesn’t reflect how real wireless signals behave in a moving, obstructed, high-density environment. That gap is exactly the kind of real-world unpredictability that open radio access networks (a.k.a. O-RAN)—an open, programmable architecture behind some 4G and 5G cellular networks—were built to manage.
So why has the O-RAN standard—which is open and available to be applied well beyond 5G telecom—never been used for vehicle communications?
Solutions to the vehicle-to-everything (V2X) problem have to date relied on new networking protocols built from scratch—only to discover chicken-and-egg problems, thorny standards wars, and real signal congestion challenges at scale. 
By contrast, O-RAN allows V2X engineers to reuse the networking protocols already developed for cellular communications. O-RAN was developed assuming cellphone towers are generally fixed in place. But, as can be seen below, O-RAN accommodates mobile “towers”—cars and trucks, in this case—with little additional effort.

title: Navigating the Pivot From Tech Expert to Organizational Leader
content:
The transition from a purely technical expert or individual contributor position to a broader leadership role is one of the most challenging phases in a STEM career. It requires moving away from relying solely on technical excellence toward mastering systems thinking, adaptive leadership, and team alignment.
To help mid-career professionals navigate the shift, the inaugural IEEE International Leadership Conference is designed to provide attendees with practical tools to step into broader responsibility and champion an entrepreneurial mindset.
The ILC event is scheduled for 3 and 4 October in Budapest. Registration is open.
Thinking beyond technical contributions
To successfully step into a leadership role, technical professionals need to look beyond their individual output and focus on “understanding the larger system, and championing innovation by building trust and aligning new ideas with organizational goals,” says IEEE Life Senior Member Daniel Sniezek, cochair of the ILC program committee.
Because engineering decisions don’t exist in a vacuum, navigating the larger system requires recognizing how technical choices intersect with the organization’s broader business, operational, and ethical realities, Sniezek says.
By letting go of the need to be the sole technical expert and focusing instead on collaborative empowerment, he says, engineers can pivot into transformational leaders who align new initiatives with the organization’s strategic vision.
Ultimately, over the span of a career, an individual’s leadership journey evolves far beyond personal advancement to “creating a lasting legacy through the people you develop, the knowledge you share, and the innovations you inspire,” he says.

title: Google just redesigned the search box for the first time in 25 years — here’s why it matters more than you think.
content:
For a quarter century, the Google search box has been one of the most recognizable interfaces in computing: a thin white rectangle, a blinking cursor, a few typed words, and a list of blue links. On Tuesday, Google will formally retire that paradigm.
At its annual I/O developer conference, Google announced a sweeping redesign of the search box itself — the literal text field where billions of queries begin every day — transforming it from a simple keyword input into a dynamic, AI-driven conversation starter that can accept text, images, PDFs, videos, and even open Chrome tabs as inputs. The company is also merging its AI Overviews and AI Mode features into a single, seamless search flow, eliminating the friction that previously forced users to choose between a traditional results page and an AI-forward experience.
Liz Reid, Google's vice president and head of Search, called it "the biggest upgrade to our iconic search box since its debut over 25 years ago" during a press briefing on Monday.
The announcement arrived alongside a blizzard of other news — new Gemini models, a personal AI agent called Spark, an intelligent shopping cart, a reimagined developer platform — but the search box redesign may prove to be the most consequential. It is the clearest signal yet that Google views the future of its flagship product not as a place where users type fragmented keywords, but as an interface where they hold open-ended, multimodal conversations with an AI system backed by the entire web.

title: Listen Labs raises $69M after viral billboard hiring stunt to scale AI customer interviews
content:
Alfred Wahlforss was running out of options. His startup, Listen Labs, needed to hire over 100 engineers, but competing against Mark Zuckerberg's $100 million offers seemed impossible. So he spent $5,000 — a fifth of his marketing budget — on a billboard in San Francisco displaying what looked like gibberish: five strings of random numbers.
The numbers were actually AI tokens. Decoded, they led to a coding challenge: build an algorithm to act as a digital bouncer at Berghain, the Berlin nightclub famous for rejecting nearly everyone at the door. Within days, thousands attempted the puzzle. 430 cracked it. Some got hired. The winner flew to Berlin, all expenses paid.
That unconventional approach has now attracted $69 million in Series B funding, led by Ribbit Capital with participation from Evantic and existing investors Sequoia Capital, Conviction, and Pear VC. The round values Listen Labs at $500 million and brings its total capital to $100 million. In nine months since launch, the company has grown annualized revenue by 15x to eight figures and conducted over one million AI-powered interviews.

"When you obsess over customers, everything else follows," Wahlforss said in an interview with VentureBeat. "Teams that use Listen bring the customer into every decision, from marketing to product, and when the customer is delighted, everyone is."

title: Salesforce rolls out new Slackbot AI agent as it battles Microsoft and Google in workplace AI
content:
Salesforce on Tuesday launched an entirely rebuilt version of Slackbot, the company's workplace assistant, transforming it from a simple notification tool into what executives describe as a fully powered AI agent capable of searching enterprise data, drafting documents, and taking action on behalf of employees.
The new Slackbot, now generally available to Business+ and Enterprise+ customers, is Salesforce's most aggressive move yet to position Slack at the center of the emerging "agentic AI" movement — where software agents work alongside humans to complete complex tasks. The launch comes as Salesforce attempts to convince investors that artificial intelligence will bolster its products rather than render them obsolete.
"Slackbot isn't just another copilot or AI assistant," said Parker Harris, Salesforce co-founder and Slack's chief technology officer, in an exclusive interview with Salesforce. "It's the front door to the agentic enterprise, powered by Salesforce."

Harris was blunt about what distinguishes the new Slackbot from its predecessor: "The old Slackbot was, you know, a little tricycle, and the new Slackbot is like, you know, a Porsche."

The new version runs on an entirely different architecture built around a large language model and sophisticated search capabilities that can access Salesforce records, Google Drive files, calendar data, and years of Slack conversations.
"It's two different things," Harris explained. "The old Slackbot was algorithmic and fairly simple. The new Slackbot is brand new — it's based around an LLM and a very robust search engine, and connections to third-party search engines, third-party enterprise data."

For the past year, the industry narrative has focused on large language models that can write poetry or debug code. With Cowork, Anthropic is betting that the real enterprise value lies in an AI that can open a folder, read a messy pile of receipts, and generate a structured expense report without human hand-holding.

title: Show HN: GPT-4-powered web searches for developers
content:
Hi HN,

Today we’re launching GPT-4 answers on Phind.com, a developer-focused search engine that uses generative AI to browse the web and answer technical questions, complete with code examples and detailed explanations. Unlike vanilla GPT-4, Phind feeds in relevant websites and technical documentation, reducing the model’s hallucination and keeping it up-to-date. To use it, simply enable the “Expert” toggle before doing a search.

GPT-4 is making a night-and-day difference in terms of answer quality. For a question like “How can I RLHF a LLaMa model”, Phind in Expert mode delivers a step-by-step guide complete with citations (https://phind.com/search?cache=0fecf96b-0ac9-4b65-893d-8ea57...) while Phind in default mode meanders a bit and answers the question very generally (https://phind.com/search?cache=dd1fe16f-b101-4cc8-8089-ac56d...).

GPT-4 is significantly more concise and “systematic” in its answers than our default model. It generates step-by-step instructions over 90% of the time, while our default model does not.

We’re particularly focused on ML developers, as Phind can answer questions about many recent ML libraries, papers, and technologies that ChatGPT simply cannot. Even with ChatGPT’s alpha browsing mode, Phind answers technical questions faster and in more detail.

For example, Phind running on “Expert” GPT-4 mode can concisely and correctly tell you how to run an Alpaca model using llama.cpp: (https://phind.com/search?cache=0132c27e-c876-4f87-a0e1-cc48f...). In contrast, ChatGPT-4 hallucinates and writes a make function for a fictional llama.cpp.
